senses.definition: Full of merriment and high spirits; jovial; joyous; merry.

quotes.text: "Full jolly Knight he seemed […] full large of limb and every joint / He was, and cared not for God or man a point."
quotes.reference: 1590, Edmund Spenser, “Book I, Canto II”, in The Faerie Queene. […], London: […] [John Wolfe] for William Ponsonbie, →OCLC, , stanzas xi-xii:

quotes.text: "A jolly place," said he, "in times of old! / But something ails it now: the spot is curst. ..."
quotes.reference: 1815, William Wordsworth, Hart-Leap Well, Part Second:

quotes.text: […] he is swelled into jolly dimensions by frequent potations of malt liquors […]
quotes.reference: 1819, Washington Irving, “The Stage Coach”, in The Sketch Book of Geoffrey Crayon, Gent.:

quotes.text: Jo silently notices how white and small her hand is and what a jolly servant she must be to wear such sparkling rings.
quotes.reference: 1852 March – 1853 September, Charles Dickens, chapter 16, in Bleak House, London: Bradbury and Evans, […], published 1853, →OCLC:

senses.definition: (UK, often humorous) A pleasure trip or excursion; especially, an expenses-paid or unnecessary one.

quotes.text: If you know what it means to be a “fidlet” going for a “jolly” in your “doo”, then you are part of an exclusive club that speaks colloquial Antarctic English.
quotes.reference: 2024 June 20, Eva Corlett, “Fidlets, fingies and riding a doo: study sheds light on Antarctic English slang”, in The Guardian:

senses.definition: (slang, dated) A marine in the English navy.

quotes.text: I'm a Jolly — 'Er Majesty's Jolly — soldier an' sailor too!
quotes.reference: 1896, Rudyard Kipling, Soldier an' Sailor Too:

senses.definition: (slang, archaic) A word of praise, or favorable notice.

quotes.text:
'We just need to chuck him a jolly.'
'I beg your pardon?' said Faber.
'Chuck a jolly... you know! Get people on the street talking about how amazing the show is! Tell them the tickets are sold out for the next two weeks.'
quotes.reference: 2021, Jenni Spangler, The Incredible Talking Machine:

quotes.text: Indeed it is nearly impossible to conceive how the small jolly they were in could have escaped destruction for a single instant.
quotes.reference: 1838, [Edgar Allan Poe], The Narrative of Arthur Gordon Pym of Nantucket. […], New York, N.Y.: Harper & Brothers, […], →OCLC:

examples: It’s jolly hot in here, isn’t it?

quotes.text: “Put these on,” said Carrot firmly, anticipating resistance. “What is it?” said Catweazle in horror. “Coms. Combinations. A vest and long pants all in one,” explained Carrot. “They're jolly warm.”
quotes.reference: 1970, Richard Carpenter, Catweazle, Harmondsworth: Puffin Books, page 127:

quotes.text: He'll think about paint and he'll think about glue / What a jolly boring thing to do
quotes.reference: 1971, David Bowie, “Andy Warhol”, in Hunky Dory:

quotes.text: Adrian thought it worth while to try out his new slang. ‘I say, you fellows, here's a rum go. Old Biffo was jolly odd this morning. He gave me a lot of pi-jaw about slacking and then invited me to tea. No rotting! He did really.’
quotes.reference: 1991, Stephen Fry, chapter III, in The Liar, London: William Heinemann, →ISBN, page 26:

senses.definition: (transitive, informal, archaic) To praise or talk up.

quotes.text: I do not believe in 'jollying' and 'soft soaping' a man when his work is really bad.
